items.title: Moral panics
items.claim: Stanley Cohen's Folk Devils and Moral Panics (1972) studied which group?

options.text: Mods and rockers at English seaside resorts in 1964

items.reveal_title: Bank holiday disturbances at Clacton and Brighton
items.reveal:
Cohen analysed how relatively minor incidents in 1964 were amplified by press coverage, generating reactions out of proportion to the original events.

The model has since been applied to repeated panics around drugs, immigration and youth culture.
items.why: Cohen's framework still organises how sociologists study media-driven public reactions.

items.title: UK household structure today
items.claim: What proportion of UK households in 2022 were single-person households according to the Office for National Statistics?
items.reveal_title: Roughly three in ten UK households are one person
items.reveal:
ONS data for 2022 reported around 30% of households contained a single person. The figure has risen steadily since the 1960s.

The 'standard' nuclear family is now a minority household type.
items.why: Demographic change reshapes assumptions built into policy and earlier sociological theory.

items.title: Goffman's dramaturgy
items.claim: Erving Goffman's The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life (1959) used what extended metaphor to analyse social interaction?

options.text: Theatrical performance with front-stage and back-stage

items.reveal_title: Life as performance with managed appearances
items.reveal:
Goffman drew on theatre to describe 'front' (managed self) and 'back' (off-stage) regions. His later work on stigma (1963) and institutions (1961) extended the framework.

The approach is now standard in microsociology.
items.why: Theatrical metaphors gave sociology vocabulary for the moment-to-moment work of social life.
